title: Add event-driven RAG tool-adapter quickstart (Go + TS shims + telemetry)
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: provide a compact, production-minded quickstart demonstrating an event-driven 'tool caller' adapter for RAG pipelines. Many teams wire tool-calling directly into the agent loop which creates blocking dependencies and brittle retry semantics. This quickstart introduces a small Go microservice that receives 'tool invocation' events via an internal command bus (HTTP + Redis stream) and a lightweight TypeScript dev shim that routes tool results back into the RAG orchestrator. The goal is to show a pattern that is resilient to retries, supports idempotency, and separates long-running tool work from token-sensitive model requests.

What this PR adds (summary):
- new quickstart at quickstarts/rag-evented-tool-adapter/ with step-by-step README, architecture notes, and troubleshooting guide
- Go service (cmd/adapter/main.go) implementing an event consumer, idempotency store, and simple plugin interface for HTTP and shell-backed tools
- TypeScript shim (dev-shim/) that demonstrates local dev integration with Redwood SDK (streaming + function calling) and a replay mode for deterministic tests
- Docker Compose manifest and a lightweight local Redis + MinIO dev environment for persistence and event replay
- Honeycomb telemetry preset and tracing example (OTEL) showing span correlation between agent requests and tool executions
- CI workflow that runs the quickstart smoke test and TypeScript unit tests on push

Checklist: 
- [x] README with step-by-step quickstart and 'why this pattern' section
- [x] Minimal Go example (well-documented, < 400 LOC)
- [x] TypeScript shim for local dev and tests
- [x] Local dev compose for Redis/MinIO + example seed data
- [x] CI job that verifies the smoke flow end-to-end
- [x] Telemetry example with Honeycomb keys redacted and instructions for customers

How to try locally (excerpt):
1. git checkout feature/rag-evented-tool-adapter-quickstart
2. cd quickstarts/rag-evented-tool-adapter && cp .env.example .env && set YOUR_HONEYCOMB_KEY
3. docker-compose up --build redis minio adapter shim || (use the 'dev' script in package.json for shim)
4. POST a sample RAG invocation to the shim endpoint (curl examples included)
5. Watch adapter logs for tool execution and observe spans in Honeycomb (optional)

Design notes (in-README): single-responsibility adapter, at-least-once delivery with idempotency keys, event versioning, and simple retry/backoff policy. The README highlights tradeoffs vs synchronous tool-calling and why separating tool execution helps maintain low token latency and predictable model costs. Links to related docs and reference designs are included (internal design RFC ENG-8124).

Related: ENG-8124 (design RFC), ENG-8199 (telemetry cookbook), SUP-1372 (customer ask to demonstrate long-running tool resilience).

release_notes: Add new quickstart: event-driven RAG tool-adapter (Go + TypeScript shim) demonstrating resilient tool-calling patterns, idempotency, and telemetry correlation. Useful for teams integrating long-running external tools without blocking model inference.
